topic: Machine-level programming with x86-64 assembly for code analysis
explanation: Machine-level programming involves writing code directly in assembly language, which interacts directly with the computer's hardware. Understanding assembly allows for fine-grained control over system resources, performance optimization at the hardware level, and deep analysis of compiled code.  This is crucial for systems programming, where efficient interaction with the operating system and hardware is essential.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
.section .text
.global my_func
my_func:
    ; Standard Prologue (Analysis Focus)
    push rbp         ; Save old Frame Pointer
    mov rbp, rsp     ; Set new Frame Pointer

    ; Data Movement & Arithmetic
    ; RDI = Arg1, RSI = Arg2
    mov rax, rdi     ; rax = Arg1 (Return register)
    sub rax, rsi     ; rax = Arg1 - Arg2
    mov rcx, 0xA     ; Constant
    cmp rax, rcx     ; Compare (sets FLAGS)
    jl .L_Less_Than  ; Conditional jump

.L_Continue:
    ; Epilogue
    mov rsp, rbp     ; Deallocate stack frame
    pop rbp          ; Restore old frame
    ret

.L_Less_Than:
    add rax, 1       ; rax++
    jmp .L_Continue
keywords: x86-64 assembly, low-level programming, machine code analysis, systems programming
